section_summary: This section is dominated by late-November 1943 Domei bulletins conveying Japanese wartime propaganda about Bougainville, the Gilbert Islands, the Greater East Asia Co-Prosperity Sphere, Subhas Chandra Bose, and political developments in occupied Asia. It then contains U.S. Embassy translations and analyses of Japanese newspapers published in Buenos Aires, followed by duplicate 1944 despatches concerning the limited distribution of the Nippon Times in Sweden. The section closes with a 1941 State Department memorandum retaining an anti-Roosevelt cartoon from the Japan Times and Advertiser for possible diplomatic use.

subfiles.title: Bulletin d'informations, Agence Domei, 18 November 1943
subfiles.about: Reports Japanese combat claims in the South Pacific and the activities of Subhas Chandra Bose in Nanking.
subfiles.summary: The bulletin claims Japanese attacks on Allied shipping and aircraft near Torokina, New Guinea and Balalae Island. It also notes recruitment of Indian National Army volunteers from Java and describes Subhas Chandra Bose's ceremonial and official visits in Nanking, including meetings with General Shunroku Hata and Ambassador Masayuki Tani.

subfiles.title: The Domei News, 18 November 1943
subfiles.about: Combines labor and propaganda items with an inflated estimate of American naval casualties around Bougainville.
subfiles.summary: Domei News, November 18, 1943: technical training for Malaccan youths, Tojo's speech to a Greater East Asia newspaper assembly, and a naval commentator's estimate of 18,000-20,000 American losses near Bougainville from assumed ship complements.

subfiles.title: Bulletin d'informations, Agence Domei, 20 November 1943
subfiles.about: Reports combat claims and the closing proceedings of the Greater East Asia Press Conference in Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: Domei bulletin, November 20, 1943: claimed air successes near Wewak, a Thai antiaircraft action, and mostly the Tokyo press conference creating a Greater East Asia press confederation supporting Axis aims and Indian independence, with receptions hosted by Shigemitsu and Aoki.

subfiles.title: The Domei News, 19 November 1943
subfiles.about: Presents a strategic commentary on the Solomons alongside civic and propaganda items from the Philippines and Manchukuo.
subfiles.summary: Domei News, November 19, 1943: a commentator says Allied island-hopping toward Rabaul and New Guinea exhausts America; President Laurel plants vegetables for Farmers' Day; POW broadcasts from Hsinking; Rizal Day plans and a Kalibapi tree-planting campaign.

subfiles.title: The Domei News, 20 November 1943
subfiles.about: Collects occupation news from Malaya, China, the Philippines and Java with Japanese South Pacific combat claims.
subfiles.summary: Domei News, November 20, 1943: officer training at Kampong Bahru, anti-Communist operations in northern China, Indian National Army benefits, the Manila consulate-general's inauguration, Italian Fascists freed from surveillance in Java, and claimed defense of Fakfak and raids on Funafuti and Torokina.

subfiles.title: Bulletin d'informations, Agence Domei, 22 November 1943
subfiles.about: Reports Japanese air raids in the South Pacific and political and civic news from Hsinking and Manila.
subfiles.summary: The bulletin claims destructive Japanese raids on Allied positions at Torokina and Funafuti. It records Wang Kemin's meetings with senior Manchukuo officials in Hsinking. It also describes Kalibapi's projected planting of one million fruit trees for Rizal Day and reports its claimed membership totals by Philippine province.

subfiles.title: Greater East Asia Conference Declaration
subfiles.from: Agence Domei / Greater East Asia Conference
subfiles.about: Provides a French rendering of the declaration adopted by Japan and its Asian satellite governments in Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: Greater East Asia Conference Declaration blames British and American aggression and pledges cooperation until Western power leaves East Asia, with five principles: security, mutual sovereignty, cultural development, economic cooperation and abolishing racial discrimination.

subfiles.title: Bulletin d'informations, Agence Domei, 22 November 1943
subfiles.about: Reports the opening fighting on Makin and Tarawa and diplomatic or consular movements across Asia.
subfiles.summary: Domei bulletin, November 22, 1943: headquarters acknowledges American landings on Makin and Tarawa while claiming fierce fighting continues; Bose leaves Shanghai, Sukarno travels to Nagoya, more consulates in the Philippines, Hasegawa meets Tojo, and the Thai delegation returns.

subfiles.title: Joint Declaration of the Countries of Greater East Asia
subfiles.about: States in English the ideological principles adopted at the Greater East Asia Conference.
subfiles.summary: Joint Declaration of Greater East Asia: blames the U.S. and British Empire for oppressing Asia and pledges mutual assistance, sovereignty, cultural development, economic reciprocity and friendly world relations; the page ends in the fifth principle.

subfiles.title: The Domei News, 23 November 1943
subfiles.about: Covers cultural events in Shōnan and speeches by Subhas Chandra Bose and Rash Behari Bose in Manila and Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: Domei News, November 23, 1943: Japanese-Chinese concerts, Subhas Bose's reception as Philippine state guest, and Rash Behari Bose urging Indians to join the Axis-supported struggle and predicting British and American defeat.

subfiles.title: Bulletin d'informations, Agence Domei, 24 November 1943
subfiles.about: Summarizes speeches by Subhas Chandra Bose and Joseph Laurel at a Manila state dinner.
subfiles.summary: Domei, November 24, 1943: Bose condemns British imperialism, warns American imperialism is replacing it, praises the Greater East Asia Assembly and says Indians will die for liberation; Laurel welcomes him; the Philippine National Assembly opens.

subfiles.title: The Domei News, 24 November 1943
subfiles.about: Reports sporting and language activities in Malaya, Japanese operations near Bougainville and medical cooperation with Germany.
subfiles.summary: Domei News, November 24, 1943: Shonan sports delegation touring Malaya, Ismail bin Suleiman's Japanese-speaking prize, claimed defeat of an Allied attack near Torokina and raids on Bougainville, and a Nippon Times editorial on Japanese-German medical cooperation.

subfiles.title: Bulletin d'informations, Agence Domei, 25 November 1943
subfiles.about: Reports Asian leaders' travels, an air battle near Chittagong and President Laurel's legislative program.
subfiles.summary: Domei, November 25, 1943: Ba Maw returns to Rangoon, Bose to Shonan, Free India thanks Thailand, claimed fighters downed three aircraft near Chittagong, and Laurel opens the National Assembly asking legislation on health, policing, transport, taxes, a central bank and welfare.

subfiles.title: The Domei News, 25 November 1943
subfiles.about: Combines cultural and military news with an extended report on Laurel's address to the Philippine National Assembly.
subfiles.summary: Domei News, November 25, 1943: a Filipino Pagliacci in Manila, a claimed Japanese victory near Xiangyuan, and Laurel's exposition of the Greater East Asia declaration and legislative agenda: self-sufficiency, peace and order, transport, taxation, reorganization and war-victim relief.

subfiles.title: Bulletin d'informations, Agence Domei, 29 November 1943
subfiles.about: Claims major Japanese naval victories in the Gilbert Islands and reports a Japanese diplomatic conference in Nanking.
subfiles.summary: Domei, November 29, 1943: claims Japanese submarines and aircraft sank five carriers and two cruisers west of the Gilberts on November 25-27 while admitting communications with Makin and Tarawa ceased; names three Gilbert air battles; Ambassador Tani convenes Japanese ministers and consuls after the Sino-Japanese treaty.

subfiles.title: The Domei News, 29 November 1943
subfiles.about: Reports an Indonesian history project, plans for Bose monuments and extravagant Japanese claims about American carrier losses.
subfiles.summary: Domei News, November 29, 1943: Poerbatjaraka prepares a Javanese history from an Indonesian viewpoint; army artists plan Bose and Malaya victory monuments; inflated Gilbert loss claims and commentary that Nimitz's carrier force is crippled.

subfiles.title: The Domei News, 27 November 1943
subfiles.about: Describes the transfer of a salt company to Chinese control and Philippine campaigns concerning Rizal, Tagalog and Kalibapi.
subfiles.summary: Domei News, November 27, 1943: the Central China Salt Industry Company is transferred to Chinese shareholders as revised occupation policy; Rizal birthplace shrine fund, Tagalog for the National Assembly, and Camilo Osias's Kalibapi drive to enroll 3.6 million Filipinos in 1944.

subfiles.title: The Domei News, 30 November 1943
subfiles.about: Collects Japanese military, diplomatic and Axis-solidarity items, including further claims from Burma and the Gilbert Islands.
subfiles.summary: Domei News, November 30, 1943: admirals honored, Manchukuo foreign minister Li Shaogeng quoted, claimed air victories at Feni and Akola, supposed Gilbert Islands losses, an Axis athletic rally at Meiji Shrine Stadium, a Nazi Party visit to Yasukuni, and a torpedo attack on Makin shipping.

subfiles.title: Nanking reports for 30 November 1943
subfiles.about: Reports a Nanking reception and the conclusion of a Japanese diplomatic conference in China.
subfiles.summary: Nanking reports, November 30, 1943: the Manchukuo embassy's reception on the third anniversary of the Japan-China-Manchukuo declaration, and Kumaichi Yamamoto closes the Japanese ministers and consuls conference.

subfiles.title: Translations from the Japanese Press of Buenos Aires, 1–4 November 1943
subfiles.from: Gerald Warner, U.S. Embassy, Buenos Aires
subfiles.to: Military and Naval Attachés; Department of State; Office of Strategic Services
subfiles.about: Translates and comments on items from El Nichia Djidji covering the first four days of November 1943.
subfiles.summary: Buenos Aires translations, November 1-4, 1943: the Japanese-Nanking alliance treaty and propaganda, combat claims in the South Pacific, China and New Guinea, civil defense, cabinet changes, and Moscow and American labor commentary; Warner adds skeptical parentheticals exposing inconsistencies.

subfiles.title: Translations from the Japanese Press of Buenos Aires, 26–30 November 1943
subfiles.from: Gerald Warner, U.S. Embassy, Buenos Aires
subfiles.to: Military and Naval Attachés; Office of Strategic Services
subfiles.about: Translates and annotates late-November Japanese newspaper reports printed in Buenos Aires.
subfiles.summary: The translated items range from Japanese claims about Bougainville, China, Burma and the Gilbert Islands to Chandra Bose's plans for India and renamed Andaman and Nicobar islands. Other entries concern diplomatic commentary, radio broadcasts to South America and movements within the Japanese community in Argentina. Warner again adds sardonic notes exposing contradictions, especially the reappearance of American carriers supposedly sunk in earlier Japanese reports. The report ends with details of Sadao Ando's scholarship foundation for second-generation Japanese Argentines.

subfiles.title: CIO Report No. 13497: Coverage of International News by the Japanese Press of Argentina
subfiles.from: Hugh Millard, U.S. Embassy, Buenos Aires
subfiles.about: Assesses international-news coverage in Argentina's three Japanese-language newspapers during November and December 1943.
subfiles.summary: Millard's CIO Report 13497: Argentina's Japanese papers relied on Domei Spanish transmissions and shortwave, stressing inflated American naval losses, the Greater East Asia conference, raid preparations, mobilization and reinterpreting the war's origins, plus commentary on Argentina, Bolivia, repatriates, the Balkans and repeal of Chinese exclusion.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 3662: Japanese Newspaper on Sale in Sweden, confirmation copy
subfiles.from: Herschel V. Johnson, American Legation, Stockholm
subfiles.about: Reports the unsolicited or poorly selling distribution of the Nippon Times to Swedish booksellers and subscribers.
subfiles.summary: Despatch 3662: Consul Riggs obtained April 1944 issues and a wrapper from a Malmo bookseller showing the Nippon Times was sent directly from Japan; another Malmo firm too, while a Stockholm agency had few subscribers and copies may have come via Russia; Swedish demand was tiny.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 3662: Japanese Newspaper on Sale in Sweden, filed copy and wrapper
subfiles.from: Herschel V. Johnson, American Legation, Stockholm
subfiles.about: Duplicates the Stockholm despatch and includes the mailing wrapper used to send the Nippon Times from Tokyo to Malmö.
subfiles.summary: Filed copy of Despatch 3662: two Malmo booksellers got the Nippon Times directly from Japan with little interest in selling it, and a Stockholm agency had few subscribers; the wrapper names A/B Edvin Lundgren, Sodergatan 3, Malmo, and Nippon Times Ltd., Tokyo.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on anti-Roosevelt cartoon in the Japan Times and Advertiser
subfiles.from: Division of Far Eastern Affairs, Department of State
subfiles.about: Directs that an offensive cartoon of the U.S. president be retained in case Japan protests American cartoons of its emperor.
subfiles.summary: Memo on Tokyo despatch 5196 (December 11, 1940) with an objectionable Roosevelt effigy cartoon from the Japan Times and Advertiser; Far Eastern Affairs kept it as possible evidence against Japanese complaints about the emperor's portrayal in the American press.
